name: Private Access Tokens and PACT
plain: A signed token proves the visitor is probably a real device without revealing who they are.
meaning: Privacy Pass (RFC 9576 to 9578) tokens issued after device or account attestation. Apple PAT ships in Safari and Cloudflare Turnstile consumes tokens. PACT was announced on 2026-06-22 by Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and Shopify; Apple was not listed.

web.api: Privacy Pass PrivateToken challenge in WWW-Authenticate; PAT

safari.note: Private Access Tokens for iOS 16 and macOS 13

limits.headline: Can check that you are probably a real device without learning who you are
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a site asks your browser to prove it is genuine
can: Receive a signed token showing a real Apple device or account vouched for you
Skip a CAPTCHA or other challenge for you
Accept the same token without knowing which device made it
cannot: Learn your name, device model or account from the token
Track you from token to token, since they are made to be unlinkable
Work in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Samsung Internet today
Prove you are human with certainty, only that a trusted device vouched
limits.differs: Only Safari on Mac and iPhone issues these tokens today. A cross vendor version called PACT was announced in June 2026.

story.what_it_is: A signed token that proves you are probably a real device, without telling the site who you are.

marketing.name: Private Access Tokens
marketing.pitch: Lets sites skip CAPTCHAs by checking quietly that a real Apple device is visiting, without learning who you are.

marketing.name: Private Access Tokens
marketing.pitch: Cloudflare says these tokens remove CAPTCHAs on iPhones and Macs while keeping visitors private.

story.for_you: On supported Apple devices you see fewer puzzles asking you to pick traffic lights. Your phone proves itself in the background. You never see the check.
story.for_makers: Makers get a strong sign that the visitor is a real device, and not a bot farm, with no extra data to store. It cuts fraud and friction. Sites need a provider such as Cloudflare to issue and check tokens.

use_cases.example: A shop behind Cloudflare skips the puzzle for iPhone shoppers, so more people finish checkout and bots still have to solve harder tests.
A browser game's sign up page checks for a real device token, so one person cannot make hundreds of free accounts for cheating.
A social site lets verified devices post and follow right away, and challenges unverified ones with extra steps.
An ad network discounts clicks that come without a token on devices that normally have one, which reduces click fraud.
A login page uses the token to lower friction for real devices and raise it for scripts that try thousands of passwords.
A news site limits scraping by asking for a token before it serves full articles to automated visitors.
A person who finds image puzzles hard to solve gets in with no puzzle, because the device proves itself in the background.

technical_bounds: Issuers can see attestation requests; issuer collusion is the main risk
PACT is only announced; shipping status unverified

value.abuse: Attestation could exclude minority browsers or devices

history.change: RFC 9576 to 9578 Privacy Pass published (Jun 2024 per IETF)
PACT announced by Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla, Shopify
